title: The signing session
summary: A signing session at the club shop. The man at the front has forty photos and he's selling them online. Behind him, a girl with one programme. You've got fifteen minutes. A season on, the programme comes back.

ends.title: Her programme
ends.text: At a signing session you stopped signing a dealer's forty photos so a girl at the back could get her one. She still has the programme. He still sells photos.

ends.title: Forty photos
ends.text: You signed forty photos for a man who sold them by teatime. The girl behind him got your name on her programme as you were leaving.

beats.title: Fifteen minutes

event.title: Fifteen minutes
event.speaker: kidfan
setup: The club shop, fifteen minutes, a queue out of the door. The man at the front has forty photos of you in a folder, all the same. Three places back, {kidfan.name} is holding one programme with both hands.

say: The man slides the photos across one at a time. You've done eleven. The shop manager taps his watch. The girl is watching the clock on the wall.

replies.label: "That's enough for you, mate." Wave the girl forward.
Keep signing, and catch the girl at the door after.

stop.text: He argues. The queue doesn't take his side. The girl gets her programme signed and asks you to write "to my nan" as well. You do.

forty.text: Forty photos. They're online for twenty quid each by teatime. The queue gets cut off two people before the girl.

after.text: You find her at the door. She's been crying a bit. You sign the programme on the shop window, and the cover's a bit bent now.

beats.hint: A signing session at the club shop

event.title: The programme
event.speaker: kidfan
setup: A season on, at the barrier. {kidfan.short} has the same programme in a plastic sleeve. "My nan died," she says. "She had this by her bed. I wanted you to know."

choices.label: Sign it again, under the first one.

outcomes.text: You write "for your nan" under the first signature. She holds it to her chest and goes.
She's got your name on the back, from the door, as you left. You sign the front. "She'd have liked that," she says.
She tells you about her nan for five minutes. The man with the folder is at the other end of the barrier. You don't go over.
She tells you about her nan. You think about the forty photos.
